event: Thursday: dawn at the boathouse, the register, the whistle; fewer shriekers on the shingle today.
Shiv signs "Doyle (reluctant, again)"; you two swim out to the buoy and hang there, breathing.

memory.fact: Shiv signed the swimmers' register under Nala again: Doyle (reluctant, again).

event: Shiv says the swimming's fine; it's the register she minds. "Feels like being counted."

event: Ten: History in the Long Room; Kit sits beside you, composed, as if last night was nothing.
The lecture is the old trials of cunning-women, which ended in 1736; the room goes quiet for it.

memory.fact: History of Magic's second week covers the old trials of cunning-women, which ended in 1736.

event: The lecturer gives a date as 1763; Kit writes 1736 in your margin and underlines it twice.

memory.fact: When the History lecturer said 1763, Kit wrote 1736 in Nala's margin and underlined it twice.

event: Halfway through she slides you a note: "Bus at 6. Film at 7. I'll choose. You'll hate it."
You write under it, "I'll love it," and slide it back; she folds it very small and keeps it.

memory.fact: Kit's note to Nala: Bus at 6. Film at 7. I'll choose. You'll hate it. Nala wrote: I'll love it.

event: Lunch: Amara has debating in the Great Hall annexe; Priya drags you along to watch.

memory.fact: Priya took Nala from lunch to watch Amara debate; Amara had practised on Priya all week.

event: Amara argues that a spell belongs to the focus, and wins the room in four minutes flat.

memory.fact: Amara won her first debate, that a spell belongs to its focus, in four minutes; it wasn't close.

event: After, she finds you at the door, bright from winning: "Freckles. You came to watch me."
"Priya brought me." "Mm," says Amara. "But you stayed." She tucks your hair behind your ear.

memory.fact: After debating Amara tucked Nala's hair behind her ear: you came to watch me; but you stayed.

event: "You and Ashworth," Amara says lightly, watching your face. "Notes in History. I saw."
You say Kit's your friend. Amara smiles slowly: "Lucky Ashworth," and walks off to her next class.

memory.fact: Amara saw Nala and Kit pass notes in History; told Kit's her friend, she said: Lucky Ashworth.

event: Two: the Practice Hall and the warming charm; you take your stone and remember Lin's words.
You breathe out as you draw the spiral, loose, and call the heat in slowly, on the breath.
The stone warms in your palm, steadily, to bathwater-warm, and holds there; no blood, no headache.

memory.fact: Drawing on the out-breath, Nala warmed her stone bathwater-warm and steady, with no nosebleed.

event: The demonstrator passes, touches the stone with two fingers, and nods: "That's the way."
Bea, at the next bench, gets her stone faintly warm for the first time and squeaks; you both laugh.

memory.fact: Bea got her warming-charm stone faintly warm for the first time, and she and Nala laughed.
Bea got her warming-charm stone faintly warm for the first time, and she and Nala laughed.

event: Across the hall Lin's stone is warm already; she catches your eye and breathes out, slowly, smiling.
Quarter to seven: a soft knock on 14; Lin, sketchbook hugged to her chest, very pale.
"Life drawing," she says. "It's my first one. Would you walk me over? Just to the door."
You walk her across the quad to the Drawing Room; its windows glow with lamplight.

memory.fact: Life drawing meets Thursdays at seven in the Drawing Room, under lamps in place of the skylights.

event: At the door she stops; you tell her you'll be in the library finishing your essay, after.

event: Lin nods, breathes out the way she taught you, and goes in, and the door closes behind her.

memory.fact: Nala walked Lin to her first life drawing; at the door Lin breathed out slowly, and went in.
Nala walked Lin to her first life drawing; at the door Lin breathed out slowly, and went in.

event: The library reading room: green lamps, long oak tables; Kit is already there, and moves her books.
You write your essay's last pages across from her, in silence, Lin's soft nib in your pen.
At nine Lin comes in, pink to the ears, and sits beside you with her sketchbook shut on her knee.
"The model sat nude," she whispers. "A second-year. Two hours. I drew her eleven times."

memory.fact: At life drawing a second-year sat nude for two hours, and Lin drew her eleven times.

event: She opens the book: quick, fluid, beautiful drawings, a woman in charcoal again and again.
Kit leans over, looks a long while, and says, quite seriously, "These are very good."

memory.fact: Lin's life drawings are quick, fluid and alive; Kit looked a long while and called them very good.
Lin's life drawings are quick, fluid and alive; Kit looked a long while and called them very good.

event: Lin goes pinker; then, to you, very low: "I'd like to draw you. Sometime. If you'd sit."
"Yes," you say. Lin looks at her hands. "Clothed. To start." Kit stares hard at her book.

memory.fact: Lin asked to draw Nala sometime, and Nala said yes; clothed, Lin said, to start.
Lin asked to draw Nala sometime, and Nala said yes; clothed, Lin said, to start.

event: Kit leaves at ten with a nod; Lin leaves at half past, touching your shoulder on her way.
You write the last line near midnight: intent comes from wherever the wanting lives.

memory.fact: Nala finished her essay near midnight; its last line: intent comes from wherever the wanting lives.

event: Walking back, you look across the quad: every window dark but one, the infirmary lamp.
You stand in the cold a moment, looking at it, thinking of Yusra at her desk with her book.
Then you go up to Thornfield; Bea's door is shut, her lamp out, and you go quietly past it.
You put the finished essay on your desk under Kit's handkerchief, and sleep at once.
